notes: Fixtures under fixtures/<repo>/ are placed at the work repo root. Every assertion a program can decide is graded by checks.py; the rest go to the model grader. Executors are told to install nothing, so 'asks before installing' is graded from the answer and the raw log.

evals.name: fresh-setup-mixed-repo
evals.prompt: I've got this little repo with a Python script, a deploy shell script, a Dockerfile, and some YAML. Set up linting for it — pick good linters for each file type and make it so they get run before any commit. I'm on a Mac.
evals.expected_output: Detects Python/Shell/Dockerfile/YAML, consults super-linter for current linters, recommends primary linters (ruff, shellcheck, hadolint, yamllint), lists install commands instead of installing, writes a ## Linting section into AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md requiring lint-before-commit, adds a `make lint` target, documents it in README, and asks whether to add a git pre-commit hook instead of adding one.
expectations: `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repo has a `## Linting` section that says to lint before committing (the section contains `commit`).
The `Makefile` has a `lint:` target whose recipe runs `ruff`, `shellcheck`, `hadolint`, and `yamllint`.
The raw log shows a fetch of the super-linter README (a command naming `super-linter`), or the answer says it used the offline fallback.
No git hook was added: no `.githooks/` directory, no `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and no `core.hooksPath` change.
No installer ran (no `brew install`, `pipx install`, `pip install`, or `npm install -g` command in the raw log), and the answer lists an install command for each linter that is missing.
The answer asks whether the user wants a git pre-commit hook (a line naming `hook` that ends in `?`).

evals.name: scoped-new-filetypes
evals.prompt: I'm about to start adding Terraform modules and a few bash scripts to this repo. Before I do, set me up with the right linters for those and make running them a required step before I commit.
evals.expected_output: Scopes to Terraform and Shell (does not try to lint every file type in the repo), uses super-linter to pick tflint and shellcheck, gives install + run commands, writes the lint-before-commit expectation into the agent guide, adds make lint. Mentions optional extras (checkov/trivy) without forcing them.
expectations: `AGENTS.md` or `CLAUDE.md` in the repo has a `## Linting` section that says to lint before committing (the section contains `commit`).
The `Makefile` `lint:` target runs `tflint` and `shellcheck`, and runs no Python or Markdown linter (`ruff`, `pylint`, `flake8`, `markdownlint`).
The answer names `checkov` or `trivy` as an optional extra, and neither appears in the `Makefile`.
No git hook was added: no `.githooks/` directory, no `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, and no `core.hooksPath` change.

evals.name: single-language-claude-md
evals.prompt: what's the current best linter for python? add it to my CLAUDE.md so you always run it before committing my changes
evals.expected_output: Confirms the current Python linter (ruff) against super-linter, explains why, gives install + run command, and edits the existing CLAUDE.md to add a linting expectation that the agent runs the linter before commits. Should not add unrelated linters or create a second agent guide.
expectations: The existing `CLAUDE.md` keeps its original lines and gains a `## Linting` section that contains `commit`.
The answer and the `## Linting` section name `ruff`.
The `## Linting` section names no linter for another language (`shellcheck`, `yamllint`, `hadolint`, `markdownlint`, `eslint`).
